newsitem.title: USA: Housing bonds, long-term debt on Mass. agenda.
newsitem.headline: Housing bonds, long-term debt on Mass. agenda.

text.p: Massachusetts Housing Committee plans to vote on a $375 million housing bond Tuesday afternoon.

The bill provides $220 million for renovation of existing public housing units; $75 million to assist low-income earners acquire housing; and $20 million to help keep current tenants in their low-cost housing when special mortgages that keep rents low expire under the government programs that created them.
The balance of the bond would be used for a variety of housing creation or improvement projects such as assistance to first-time homebuyers.

Meanwhile, the life of bond authorizations set to expire on June 30 would be extended for another year under terms of a bill being aired on Wednesday before the Long-Term Debt and Capital Planning Committee. The list of previously approved capital projects that are still on-going, or have yet to be launched, was filed May 13 by Gov. Weld.

By week's end, the six legislative conferees who will write the final version of an $18.3 billion state budget for the new fiscal year will likely have been named and be hard at work. ((--Boston bureau, 617-367-4106))
